Phylogenomics, spatiotemporal transcriptional dynamics and Cis-regulatory architecture underlying the Portulaca oleracea antioxidant network under extreme salinity.

This study integrates multi-tissue RNA-Seq, qRT-PCR, comparative phylogenomics across 154 plant genomes, and condition-specific gene regulatory network modeling to characterize 436 antioxidant loci in the extreme halophyte Portulaca oleracea under chronic hypersalinity. It reveals spatiotemporal transcriptional dynamics and cis-regulatory architecture coordinating antioxidant defenses across organs and developmental stages, providing a framework for understanding salinity tolerance in this xerohalophyte.

Gut microbes 2026-12-31 Medium

Deep longitudinal phenotyping of a single individual enables host-microbiome metabolic modeling over 3.6 years.

Researchers tracked one person's gut microbiome at 51 time points over 3.6 years, building time-point-specific metabolic models from metagenomic data and predicting microbial metabolic activity via flux balance analysis. They then compared microbial abundances and predicted metabolic fluxes against clinical inflammation markers like CRP, lactoferrin, and calprotectin. This deep single-subject longitudinal design links microbiome composition and metabolism to episodic colonic inflammation over time.

An integrative systems biology framework decodes peripheral blood transcriptomic signatures, systemic interactome networks, and candidate targets in lung squamous cell carcinoma.

This study applies an integrative systems-biology approach to peripheral blood transcriptomic data from lung squamous cell carcinoma (LSCC) patients, aiming to uncover systemic gene-expression signatures and construct interactome networks. The authors identify candidate hub genes that may serve as blood-based biomarkers or therapeutic targets, linking peripheral immune and systemic changes to LSCC biology.

Plant-environment interactions (Hoboken, N.J.) 2026-12-01 Low

Beyond the Primary-Secondary Dichotomy: Toward a Unified Metabolic Perspective.

This review argues that the traditional division of plant metabolism into primary and secondary categories is conceptually outdated and fails to reflect how metabolites are actually produced and function. The authors show that pathways share precursors, cofactors, regulatory mechanisms, and transport systems, and that metabolites can serve growth, signaling, defense, or stress roles depending on context. They call for a unified metabolic perspective that better captures this interconnectedness.

The Maladaptive Stress State: A Systems Framework for Chronic Disease Persistence.

This Perspective proposes the Maladaptive Stress State (MSS) as a systems-level framework to explain why biologically diverse chronic diseases converge on persistent states of chronic inflammation, impaired repair, and reduced adaptive flexibility. The framework distinguishes disease-initiating lesions from the self-sustaining maladaptive state that persists after the original insult subsides, offering a unifying conceptual model for chronic disease persistence.

Meta-finetuning foundation models for generalizable biological image segmentation in ultra-low-data regimes.

MetaTune adapts foundation models for biological image segmentation when labeled data are extremely scarce. It splits model parameters into meta-parameters that improve generalization and non-meta parameters that handle task-specific adaptation, using an iterative bi-level meta-finetuning scheme. This lets pretrained segmentation models work well with very few training examples.

Image-guided alignment of consecutive multi-modal tissue slides.

COAST is a new computational method that physically aligns consecutive tissue sections using only their microscopy images, without needing shared molecular features or prior annotations. It enables construction of unified multi-modal spatial datasets and performs comparably to established uni-modal alignment tools across different spatial transcriptomics technologies, tissues, and resolutions.

Comparison of interventional causal structure learning algorithms for gene regulatory network inference.

Cell systems 2026-11-13 High

Multi-omics-constrained kinetic models quantify pathway rewiring and predict metabolic vulnerabilities in BRCA1-deficient ovarian cancer.

The authors built near-genome-scale kinetic models of metabolism (over 2,100 reactions) constrained by multi-omics data for isogenic BRCA1 wild-type and BRCA1-mutant ovarian cancer cells. These models quantified how BRCA1 loss rewires metabolic pathways and identified 28 enzyme-mediated metabolic vulnerabilities, 24 of which map to known or approved drugs. Independent DepMap data supported the predictions, suggesting a framework for prioritizing metabolic drug targets in BRCA1-deficient cancers.

A single-nucleus transcriptomic atlas reveals the endodermal gene regulatory network underlying Arabidopsis stem gravitropism.

This study uses single-nucleus RNA sequencing to build a transcriptomic atlas of the Arabidopsis stem, revealing the endodermal gene regulatory network that controls gravitropism. The work links the gravity-sensing statocytes to the transcriptional programs that drive asymmetric growth, with SGR5/IDD15 as a key regulator. It provides a resource for understanding how plants convert gravity perception into directional growth.

PIANO enables generative modeling of gene expression and scales multi-omics integration to 100 million cells.

PIANO is a deep learning framework that uses a generative model of gene expression to integrate single-cell multi-omics data. It addresses three key challenges in data integration: correcting strong batch effects, scaling to millions of cells (demonstrated up to 100 million), and modeling how covariates influence gene expression. This enables more accurate comparisons across large-scale transcriptomic atlases.

Longevitomics as the science of the longevitome: Towards a unified systems science of healthy longevity.

The paper proposes "Longevitomics," an integrative systems-science framework for studying healthy longevity, and defines the "Longevitome" as the dynamic, multi-layered architecture of molecular, physiological, and environmental determinants of long life. It argues that longevity research has been fragmented across genomics, epigenomics, proteomics, metabolomics, microbiome science, digital phenotyping, and AI, and that these layers should be modeled together rather than in isolation. The contribution is primarily conceptual, offering a unifying vocabulary and framework rather than new data or methods.

Host-like temperature unlocks glucose uptake and metabolism in pathogenic Leptospira.

Using transcriptome-integrated genome-scale metabolic modeling, the authors show that pathogenic Leptospira grown at host-like temperature (37°C) upregulates glucose uptake and metabolism, contrary to the long-held view that this pathogen relies mainly on fatty acids. This temperature-dependent metabolic shift may reflect adaptation to the mammalian host environment.

Network inference at single-cell resolution reveals morphoregulatory divergence and multilayered buffering in limb evolution.

This study compares limb development between mice and pigs using single-cell transcriptomics and chromatin accessibility, combined with gene regulatory network inference. They find that while cellular organization is broadly conserved, specific HOX, FGF, and SHH regulatory programs diverge between species. Pharmacological FGFR inhibition in mouse limb buds mimics the pig-specific distal expansion of GREM1, suggesting that layered buffering mechanisms shape morphological evolution.

scPhyloGRN: gene regulatory network inference guided by lineage topology in single-cell developmental data.

A time-resolved single-nucleus atlas of cochlear aging reveals biphasic inflammaging and Tbx2-dependent inner hair cell maintenance.

This study builds a time-resolved single-nucleus atlas of the aging cochlea, tracking how different cell types change over time. It identifies two distinct phases of age-related inflammation (biphasic inflammaging) and shows that the transcription factor Tbx2 is required for maintaining inner hair cells. The work integrates cell-cell communication, gene regulatory networks, and bulk validation to map the molecular progression of age-related hearing loss.

Bio Systems 2026-11-01 Medium

Disagreement-informed arbitration for gene regulatory network inference: A score-level meta-classifier and a diagnostic typology of inter-method conflict.

The authors propose a meta-learning approach to gene regulatory network inference that arbitrates disagreements between ten existing inference methods on a per-edge basis, using a gradient-boosted classifier trained on the raw scores each method assigns. They also develop a diagnostic typology of inter-method conflict. Evaluated across six single-cell perturbation screens, the approach aims to outperform both single-method selection and simple averaging.

Comparative phylogenomics and transcriptional regulatory networks of AQPs, HSPs, and LEA proteins in salt-stressed Portulaca oleracea.

This study combines deep learning-based genome annotation, multi-tissue RNA-Seq, phylogenomics, and gene regulatory network inference to characterize aquaporins, heat shock proteins, and LEA proteins in the halophyte Portulaca oleracea under salt stress. The authors produce a high-quality genome annotation (58,817 genes, 96.5% BUSCO completeness) and identify 78 AQPs, 525 HSPs, and 119 LEAs, revealing their coordinated transcriptional regulation. The work provides a resource for understanding salt tolerance mechanisms in halophytes.

A pathogen-free citrus model recapitulates Huanglongbing-associated molecular and physiological reprogramming.

The authors created a pathogen-free citrus model by using virus-induced gene silencing to knock down two chloroplast biosynthesis genes (PDS and ALAD) in Citrus macrophylla, disrupting both carotenoid and chlorophyll production. This chloroplast dysfunction reproduced key molecular and physiological features of Huanglongbing (HLB), suggesting that host chloroplast breakdown—rather than the pathogen alone—drives much of the disease phenotype. The work provides a tractable system for studying HLB mechanisms without needing the unculturable bacterium.

Multi-omic analysis reveals maturation programs in human pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes during long-term culture.

This study used integrated metabolomics, proteomics, and transcriptomics to profile human pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (hPSC-CMs) over 113 days of culture, identifying molecular pathways and regulatory programs that drive maturation. The multi-omic approach reveals progressive maturation programs, offering a resource for understanding how hPSC-CMs mature in vitro. These findings could help overcome the immature phenotype that limits the translational utility of hPSC-CMs for disease modeling and regenerative medicine.

Archives of toxicology 2026-11-01 Medium

Causality analysis of toxicological mechanisms in networked systems such as adverse outcome pathway networks.

This paper argues that traditional causality frameworks like Koch's postulates and Bradford Hill criteria are insufficient for analyzing toxicological mechanisms in complex networked systems such as Adverse Outcome Pathway networks and multi-omics data. It synthesizes a modern causality toolbox—including directed acyclic graphs for making causal assumptions explicit and quantitative methods—to better handle multifactorial, nonlinear, and feedback-driven mechanisms. The work provides operational guidance for causal inference in toxicology.

Identification of metabolic vulnerabilities and synthetic lethal targets utilizing artificial intelligence-driven precision medicine.
